title: ADR-055: read-back navigation reaches a mirrored program without being typing
description:
hvir-9as sends PageUp/PageDown from a phone read-back gesture to a program that owns its own history, on a mirror whose per-session arm has lapsed, and keeps those bytes out of the desktop's terminal-input record. Both halves narrow written decisions, so they need a record before the code lands.

What it narrows:
- ADR-050:65-69 states 'Typing from the phone is an explicit act three times over. Settings must allow it, and the default is off. A mirror opens with input disabled and the user arms it per mirror.' Read-back navigation keeps the first two and drops the third. Record why the owner's permission is the boundary that matters and the per-mirror arm is not: the arm exists so a phone left unlocked in a pocket cannot type into a session, and a gesture a person is actively making on a screen they are looking at is not that risk. State the closed set of bytes this admits, which is exactly the two the shared wheel policy emits for an alternate-screen gesture, and that nothing else is ever exempt.
- ADR-050:74-76 states that main tells the owning renderer that mirror input reached its PTY and the renderer records it as terminal input, which arms ADR-019 and produces the next Ready and Push. Read-back navigation must not be recorded that way, or paging history on a phone produces a push notification about the person's own scrolling. Record the distinction and note that companion-sessions.ts:201-203 already draws the same one for resize.
- ADR-053's decision 1 says an alternate-screen session states it has no history to read back. That is false for any program holding its own history. Amend it: the emulator has no scrollback, the program may still have history, and the phone pages it the way the desktop does.

Consequences to state plainly:
- Paging a program's own history is not private to the phone. It is the same program, so the desktop's view moves too. Emulator-viewport read-back does not do this, so the two mechanisms behave differently in a way a person will notice.
- A program is free to bind PageUp and PageDown to something other than scrolling. The decision admits that: it is the same bet the desktop's wheel policy already makes, and parity with the desktop is the requirement.

End with a revisit clause naming what would justify widening the exempt set.
acceptance_criteria: docs/adr/ADR-055-*.md exists in the repo's ADR shape; npm run check-adrs passes with reciprocal relationship lines against ADR-050 and ADR-053. The record names the exact exempt byte set, states the attention distinction, and carries the shared-view consequence. No em dashes.
notes: Filed 2026-09-19 after the maintainer saw the false notice on a real phone. hvir-9as depends on this landing first, the way hvir-coq depended on ADR-054.
close_reason: ADR-055 landed in d1fda06; check-adrs passes with reciprocal lines against ADR-050 and ADR-053.

title: The phone cannot read back a session whose program owns its history, and says there is none
description:
Observed 2026-09-19 on a real phone against the 'Mayor Cairn' session: Claude Code running under tmux. The phone shows 'This program draws its whole screen, so there is no history to read back.' and a drag moves nothing. The desktop reads back the same session fine.

The notice is false. tmux holds a full history; it just holds it itself rather than in the emulator's scrollback. isAlternateScreen() is correct, but the sentence the page derives from it is not: what is true is that the EMULATOR has no scrollback, not that the SESSION has no history. ADR-053's decision 1 ('an alternate-screen session states that it has no history to read back', written 2026-09-19) is wrong as stated, and wrong in exactly the case the Companion exists for. A shell under tmux, a pager, and anything else holding its own history all land here.

Both read-back mechanisms already exist and route correctly. src/shared/terminal-wheel.ts:83-87 sends PageUp/PageDown to an alternate-screen program, which is how the desktop scrolls this session: tmux redraws with older content and the phone mirrors the redraw. That is why the phone moves only when the desktop scrolls. What is missing is that the phone cannot produce those keys for itself.

Three parts, and none of them is the emulator-viewport read-back, which is right and stays.

1. The gate. Page keys from a read-back gesture are input bytes, so ghostty-companion-pane's emitUser drops them on a disarmed mirror. Decided by the maintainer 2026-09-19: send them when the owner's mirrorInputAllowed is on, even after the per-mirror arm has lapsed, and never otherwise. Only the two navigation keys a read-back gesture produces, never typing. This is a page-side change: main's gate at companion-sessions.ts:195 is typingAllowed(), the owner's setting alone, so main already permits exactly this.

2. The attention leak, found while tracing part 1 and the reason this is P0 rather than P2. pty-supervisor.ts:402 fans every mirror write out to mirrorInputListeners, and ADR-050:74-76 says the renderer records that as terminal input, which arms ADR-019 and produces the next Ready and the next Push. Without a distinction, paging back on the phone generates a push notification because you scrolled. Read-back navigation must reach the PTY without being recorded as terminal input, the same distinction companion-sessions.ts:201-203 already draws for resize ('Resizing is not input, so the typing permission does not gate it'). This crosses the wire and reaches the supervisor's fan-out.

3. The notice. Stop claiming the session has no history. State what is true and what to do: the program keeps its own history and a drag pages it. Say nothing about arming if part 1 lands, since it will not be needed.

Known asymmetry to state somewhere a person will read it: emulator-viewport read-back is private to the phone, but paging tmux moves the desktop's view too, because it is the same program. That is inherent to history the program owns.
design: Do not solve this by giving the page its own scrollback again. The emulator-viewport read-back is correct for normal-screen sessions and stays; this adds the second mechanism for history the program owns, which the gesture policy already decides between.
acceptance_criteria: On a phone mirroring Claude Code under tmux with the owner's input permission on and the per-mirror arm lapsed, a drag pages back through tmux history and the notice does not claim there is none. With the owner's permission off, nothing is sent and the page says why. Paging back produces no terminal-input record, no Ready and no Push on the desktop. Typing still requires the per-mirror arm. Verified on a real device, not only against a fake.
notes: Supersedes part of ADR-053's decision 1 and narrows ADR-050:65-69 ('Typing from the phone is an explicit act three times over'), so it needs a record; see the sibling ADR bead. Found because the maintainer looked at a real phone, which is exactly what hvir-w00.7 exists to do.
close_reason: Landed in a4c2bb2. Page keys leave the pane on onNavigation past the arm, the wire admits navigation:true only for those two keys, main takes lease.navigate (no input fan-out, so no ADR-019 arming and no Push), and the notice states the program keeps its own history. Device verification on a real phone under tmux is still outstanding; tracked on hvir-w00.7.

title: The phone mirror always shows the desktop grid and a drag scrolls as far as the finger travels
description:
Why: on a real phone (2026-09-19) the mirror shows two different fits, the desktop grid scaled to the phone while hvir is focused and a phone-sized grid while it is Away (ADR-052). The Away fit is laggy to scroll and a resize round trip the person never asked for; the focused fit is the right one in both cases. In both fits a finger drag scrolls far less than the same travel on a desktop trackpad, so paging a Claude Code seat through its history takes dozens of swipes and reads as a hard stop.

What: (1) retire ADR-052's Away resize end to end, with a new ADR fully superseding it, so the phone always shows the desktop's grid scaled to its width and never resizes the PTY; (2) a drag delivers every report its travel earned (the per-event report cap is for wheel notches) and a fling keeps scrolling with momentum the way a trackpad does, so a flick reaches as far as it would on the desktop; (3) the mirror's own scrollback holds as much as the desktop pane's for normal-screen sessions.

Measured on the live mayor seat (Claude Code 2.1.278 fullscreen under tmux, mouse on): the program honours 1920 wheel-up reports before its history ends and a burst of 60 in one write is fully honoured, so the stop is the program's own rendered history, not the mirror's.
acceptance_criteria: Phone shows the desktop grid scaled to width while focused and while Away; no resize request leaves the phone; PtyMirrorLease has no resize verb and the supervisor no geometry source; a drag of N cells of travel emits N/3 SGR reports in one write; a fling continues to scroll after the finger lifts; offline gates pass.
close_reason: ADR-057 retires ADR-052; one fit, drag limit max(5,rows), fling, 10 MB mirror scrollback; gates green (local-host flaky only)

title: Read-back reports travel as one ordered write per gesture, not one POST per report
description: On the phone, a drag over a mouse-tracking program (tmux + Claude Code) turns each touchmove into up to five SGR wheel reports, and each report is its own fire-and-forget HTTP POST from inside the touch handler: unordered, uncoalesced, no backpressure, competing with the SSE redraw traffic each accepted notch causes. Batch: the pane emits one navigation string per gesture event, the page keeps one navigation request in flight per mirror and coalesces what arrives meanwhile into the next ordered POST, main validates the batch as a sequence of closed-set tokens and makes one PTY write. Also: the wheel controller's banked remainder is forgotten on finger lift instead of leaking into the next gesture, and the owned touch calls preventDefault so no compatibility mousedown reaches ghostty's canvas (which focuses the textarea and, with tracking on, sends an SGR press).
close_reason: Batched per-gesture navigation write, endGesture on finger lift, touch events cancelled; landed on feat/beads-panel

title: A phone mirror of a mouse-tracking session routes its gesture differently from the desktop

Evidence:
  tmux -L ds-research show -g mouse            -> mouse on
  tmux -L ds-research list-keys -T root | grep -ci ppage -> 0

With mouse on, tmux turns mouse tracking on for the PTY. The desktop's emulator watched that happen, so the shared wheel policy routes a trackpad to SGR wheel reports and the program scrolls itself. The phone's emulator never saw it: the enable sits where tmux attached, far outside any retained window, and ADR-054 names the mouse tracking family as a set it does not carry. The phone therefore found no mouse tracking, fell through to the alternate-screen route, and sent PageUp, which tmux binds nowhere in its root table and hands to the program as a keystroke it barely honours.

Same PTY, same gesture, two routes, because the two emulators believed different things about the session.
design:
ADR-056. Carry the mouse tracking family whole in the sticky-mode scan and widen ADR-055's exempt set to the wheel reports the policy synthesizes.

Whole, or not at all: the policy needs ?1006 before it will synthesize a report, so carrying the trackers without the encoding leaves a reader that knows the program tracks the mouse and cannot answer it, consuming every gesture silently. That is the failure ADR-054 predicted, and it is reached by carrying half the set.

The exempt set stays closed and stays navigation: buttons 64 and 65 only, which are wheel up and down. A press, a release, a drag report and a modified button are typing.
acceptance_criteria: A mirror of a session with tmux mouse on takes the same route as its desktop and its read-back matches. The preamble carries ?1000 ?1002 ?1003 ?1006 ?1015 after the screens, emits nothing for a program that turned tracking off, and stays within STICKY_MODE_PREAMBLE_MAX_CHARS. A wheel report reaches the PTY from a disarmed mirror without being recorded as terminal input; a press at the same position is refused at 400. Verified on a real device.
close_reason: Landed in d6be90e with ADR-056. CARRIED_MODES carries ?1000 ?1002 ?1003 ?1006 ?1015 after the screens; isTerminalReadBackNavigation covers the page keys plus wheel buttons 64/65; the preamble bound went 14 to 54. Route parity still wants confirming on the device against the tmux session; noted on hvir-w00.7.

title: A read-back drag pages at the speed a finger asks for, and loses nothing to event batching
description:
Found on a real phone 2026-09-19, paging tmux through the ADR-055 path: the read-back is jumpy and travels far more than the finger asks.

Two defects in src/shared/terminal-wheel.ts, which the desktop pane and the Companion mirror share.

1. Step distance ignores what a step costs. normalizedWheelDelta divides every route by cellHeight * LINES_PER_WHEEL_STEP, so one step is three cells of travel whether that step scrolls three rows (viewport route) or a whole screen (page route). On a 132x43 grid scaled onto a phone that is roughly 20 on-screen pixels per PageUp, so one swipe covers about thirty pages. The gain is off by more than an order of magnitude, and being quantized to whole pages is what makes it read as jumpy rather than fast.

2. The per-event clamp discards its overflow. consumeSteps banks only the sub-step fraction and then clamps whole steps to the route limit (1 on the page route), so the steps it clamped away are lost. How far a gesture travels then depends on how the browser batched touchmove rather than on the distance covered, which is the property the remainder banking directly above it exists to provide.

Decided with the maintainer 2026-09-19: fix both. A drag pays for a page with half the rows it moves, so dragging half a screen moves a screen; a notch keeps its three lines; an SGR report stands for a notch rather than a screen and keeps them too. The clamped overflow is banked rather than dropped, bounded by one event's worth so a synthetic or accelerated delta is rate limited instead of queued.
design:
The kind of gesture travels on the event as a required field rather than being sniffed from deltaMode: Chrome reports pixel deltas for plain mouse wheels on macOS, so deltaMode does not separate a notch from a finger. The touch adapter is the one place that knows a finger produced the event. This keeps ADR-053's one policy (same routes, same bytes, one decision about what a gesture means) and varies only what one step of travel costs.

Building the event from a DOM WheelEvent must read its fields explicitly: deltaY and the rest are prototype accessors, so a spread yields an empty object.
acceptance_criteria: A drag on the alternate screen sends one page key per half screen of travel and a notch still sends one per three lines; an SGR report keeps three lines on either. Steps a clamped event could not carry are delivered by the following events rather than lost, so equal distance travels equally however the browser batched it, and a single absurd delta queues no more than one event's worth. Verified on a real device against tmux.
close_reason: Landed. stepCells charges a drag half the rows it moves for a page key, a notch keeps three lines, SGR keeps three lines on either; consumeSteps banks the clamped overflow bounded by one event's worth. The gesture kind travels on the event. Feel still wants confirming in the hand; noted on hvir-w00.7.

title: Verify the phone read-back on a real device against a real session
description:
Everything in 07fd726, 3d572be and 5d1cbed is verified against faked emulators. Four behaviours have never run against the real ghostty build under a real finger, and each is the kind that passes a mocked test while being wrong in the hand:

1. Scroll direction. The adapter computes scrollLines(deltaY / cellHeight) with deltaY = lastY - currentY, verified against ghostty-web.js:4474-4481 and :5056-5062 by reading the built source. If the fake encodes the axis the same way the code does, both are wrong together and every direction test passes. A phone that scrolls backwards is the single most likely defect in this epic.

2. Feel. Touch deltas are divided by the mount's surface scale and sub-cell distance is banked rather than rounded. Whether that tracks the finger at a 132-column desktop grid scaled onto a phone is a judgement no test makes.

3. The soft keyboard. ghostty-web focuses its hidden textarea on every touchend regardless of disableStdin (ghostty-web.js:4695-4698 into :4619-4624), and the page stops that in the capture phase. If the interception misses, each flick raises the keyboard, which resizes the viewport, which asks the desktop for a new PTY grid while Away.

4. The return-to-live control: whether it appears when expected, whether one tap reaches the newest output over a grid taller than the phone, and whether it is reachable and legible at the top of the area.

Do this against a real Claude Code session (which draws on the alternate screen, so it must show the no-history notice and no control) and a real plain shell with genuine scrollback. Extend the companion-mirror-away smoke scenario where a behaviour can be pinned there; it is the only altitude in this repo where the real emulator runs.

If the feel is wrong, say so and stop rather than tuning constants: the design was chosen from an argument, not from a phone, and the maintainer reserved the right to reject it in the hand.
acceptance_criteria: A plain shell mirror scrolls back by finger in the right direction at a comfortable rate, in the session's colours. A full-screen session shows the live screen, the line 'This program keeps its own history. Drag to page back through it.', and no return-to-live control; a drag pages that program's own history (ADR-055) with the owner's permission on and the per-mirror arm lapsed, and produces no Ready and no Push on the desktop. A flick does not raise the soft keyboard. Over a grid taller than the phone, one tap on the control reaches the newest output. The companion-mirror-away smoke scenario covers whatever of this it can.
notes:
Partially executed 2026-09-19 by the maintainer looking at a real phone. It immediately found what no faked-emulator test could: for a Claude Code session under tmux, the phone showed 'no history to read back' and a drag moved nothing, while the desktop read the same session back fine. Filed as hvir-9as (P0) and hvir-14d (ADR-055); both landed 2026-09-19 (d1fda06, a4c2bb2).

Second device pass the same day found the paging gain wrong: about twenty on-screen pixels per PageUp at a scaled desktop grid, roughly thirty pages to a swipe, and the per-event clamp discarding its overflow so the same drag landed differently depending on touchmove batching. Filed and fixed as hvir-dzz (dc70a24): a drag now pays half the rows it moves for a page, a notch keeps three lines, and the clamped steps are banked. That gain was chosen from an argument again, not from a phone, so it is this bead's job to confirm half-a-screen-per-page is right in the hand.

The same pass confirmed the half-black terminal area is ADR-052 working as designed: a 132x43 grid fitted to a portrait phone by width can only be short, and the phone asks for its own grid only while the desktop is unfocused. Not a defect; possibly still a product question about a person holding their phone at their desk.

Still unverified and still this bead's job:
- scroll direction under a real finger on a NORMAL-screen session with genuine emulator scrollback. The tmux case exercises the page-key path, not the viewport path, so the direction question is untouched by either finding.
- the feel of the delta-to-rows conversion at a scaled desktop grid, and of the new half-screen-per-page gain.
- whether the capture-phase touchend interception actually stops the soft keyboard.
- the return-to-live control's appearance, reachability and one-tap behaviour over a grid taller than the phone.
- that a drag actually pages tmux from a mirror nobody armed, that the desktop gets no Ready and no Push from it, and that the desktop's own view moving with the phone is tolerable in the hand.

title: ADR-054: main carries sticky terminal modes ahead of the replayed tail
description:
hvir-coq makes main scan the PTY stream for a closed set of sticky DEC private modes and emit their state ahead of the replayed bytes. That crosses a boundary this codebase states in writing: ADR-050:50 reads 'Bytes cross from main to the phone as they are. Main does not interpret them', its rejected alternatives refuse main holding terminal state (ADR-050:123-125), and src/main/companion/companion-page-mirror.ts:9-10 restates it at the code level ('Bytes pass through untouched in both directions; nothing here logs, trims, or composes them').

Shipping the scanner without a record leaves the codebase contradicting itself, so this lands in the same wave as hvir-coq, not after it.

The record must fix the boundary precisely: main holds the on/off state of a named, closed set of modes and nothing else. No screen model, no cursor, no cell grid, no content. Name what is carried (1049 and 47, the alternate-screen family) and name what is deliberately not carried and why: synchronized output ?2026 (a dangling set would freeze the phone's first frame, so it is suppressed rather than replayed), ?1048 (save/restore cursor, an action with no steady state, which would jump the cursor mid-replay), ?1047 (unless the scanner also models that 1047l clears the screen), the mouse tracking family (carrying it makes hasMouseTracking() true and terminal-wheel.ts:60-79 then consumes every gesture as SGR reports that a disarmed mirror drops, silently disabling the phone's read-back), bracketed paste, application cursor keys, charset designation, keypad mode, DECSTBM and SGR.

Also record that the preamble is a distinct wire field, not a prefix of tail: a prefix is unshippable because sessions-companion.ts:248-249 rejects an opened event whose tail exceeds 256K and the mirror tail saturates at exactly that, and because companion-mirror-feed.ts:51,:100 re-slices the retained text from the front on every remount.

Consequences: ADR-050:101-102 ('A raw tail replays an imperfect first frame until the program redraws') is narrowed for the carried modes only; the rejected alternative at ADR-050:123-125 (a headless emulator in main) stays rejected. End with a revisit clause naming the modes left out.
acceptance_criteria: docs/adr/ADR-054-*.md exists in the repo's ADR shape and npm run check-adrs passes with reciprocal relationship lines against ADR-050. The Decision names the carried set, states the ?2026 suppression, and states the preamble is a distinct field. No em dashes.
notes: Split out of hvir-w00.2 during the 2026-09-19 grounding pass. AGENTS.md's one-decision-per-record rule forbids folding it into ADR-053. docs/design.md is a single index file, so both records and every lifecycle edit are owned by one bead in the wave to keep file sets disjoint; this bead and hvir-w00.2 must therefore be implemented by the same hand or strictly in sequence.
close_reason: Wave 1 implemented and verified: check-adrs, check-seams, lint, typecheck and the full suite (469 files, 4081 tests) pass. architecture:check is environment-blocked in this clone (scripts/architecture-github.mts requires origin jarmak-personal/hvir; this tree is sjarmak/hvir); architecture:report is clean with a budget-violation set identical to the pre-change tree.

title: Read back through the emulator's viewport and delete the page's scrollback layer
description:
Make the emulator's own viewport the phone's read-back, per ADR-053.

Delete:
- src/renderer/companion/src/companion-mirror-history.ts entire (MirrorHistory, historyText, HISTORY_LINE_LIMIT, HISTORY_REFRESH_MS) and test/companion-mirror-history.test.ts.
- The history box and its scrollback slice in companion-terminal-mount.ts: the <pre>, its font/lineHeight sizing, the scrollback() slice at :213-217, and the history's share of fit() at :230-240.
- bufferLines and CompanionBufferLine from companion-terminal-pane.ts, their implementation in ghostty-companion-pane.ts:96-105, the stub in test/companion-terminal-pane-seam.test.ts:38, and the buffer rows in test/companion-page-fixture.ts:216,258. The mount's history is the only caller; the seam conformance test pins only mount/write/resize/dispose/onData, so removing the member does not break it.
- .companion-terminal-history in styles.css:439-443, whose hardcoded #e8eaee is the epic's second observed defect.

This also retires the missing-spaces bug without fixing it. ghostty-web's translateToString concatenates getChars() per cell and returns '' for codepoint 0, never padding, so every blank cell vanishes from the string and takes its column with it (ghostty-web.js:4147). That is what produced 'Ididverifytheonethinginthatreply'. The desktop already knows: ghostty-terminal-pane.ts:759-763 builds row text cell by cell with codepoint < 32 mapped to a space. After this bead nothing in the Companion calls translateToString, so the row-text problem stops existing here rather than being solved twice.

Add:
- Touch scrolling over the grid, adapted into TerminalWheelController's event shape (pixel deltas, no modifiers) so one policy covers both gestures: normal screen moves the viewport, alternate screen sends page keys, a mouse-tracking program gets SGR reports. Synthesized bytes pass emitUser's gate unchanged, so a disarmed mirror still sends nothing.
- The empty-history state: when the session is on the alternate screen there is no scrollback, and the phone says so in a line rather than showing nothing or showing repaint frames.

Depends on hvir-coq: until sticky modes survive replay, the phone's emulator is on the normal screen for a full-screen session and the empty-history state would never be reached.
design: Net-negative diff. The mount keeps its scale transform for the case where the desktop holds a wide grid, but the extent now sizes to the grid alone. Check whether the host still needs to be a scroller once nothing is drawn above the grid.
acceptance_criteria: companion-mirror-history.ts and its test are gone; bufferLines is absent from the port, the adapter and the fixtures; typecheck and the full test suite pass. A mirror of a plain shell scrolls back through its scrollback by finger drag, in the session's colours and attributes. A mirror of a full-screen session shows the live screen and a stated reason there is no history. A disarmed mirror sends nothing on any gesture. The diff removes more lines than it adds.
notes: hvir-w00 was filed against three observed defects. The spaces are retired by deletion here; the chrome defect is dissolved by hvir-coq; the theme defect was misdiagnosed and is its own bead.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: check-adrs, check-seams, lint, typecheck and the full suite pass; the deletion is complete (no translateToString, bufferLines, MirrorHistory or .companion-terminal-history remain under the page tree except a test asserting their absence). Seven adversarial findings were confirmed and repaired by replacing the scroll seam with one reporting unconsumed distance; ten were refuted.

title: ADR-053: the Companion mirror reads back through the emulator's viewport
description:
Write the record for the read-back decision taken on 2026-09-19, before the code changes.

Decision: the phone's read-back is the emulator's own viewport. The page stops maintaining a parallel scrollback surface above the grid; scrolling moves the emulator's viewport over the scrollback it already holds, drawn by the same renderer that draws the live screen.

The reasoning to record:
- Fidelity is the point. The mirror should be a continuation of the session's screen, not a transcript of it. A shell's scrollback is columnar (ls, git log --graph, diff, tables) and reflowing it to phone width destroys the thing being read back. Drawing it through the emulator makes colour, attributes, wide characters and theme exact by construction rather than by a second renderer that will drift.
- The page's <pre> layer could not carry them at all. textContent has no colour, and the alternative (coalesced span runs, rebuilt incrementally, plus a full rebuild on every resize) is a DOM reimplementation of the emulator's drawing.
- A full-screen session has no scrollback, and the phone should say so rather than show something. This only becomes true once hvir-coq lands; before it, the phone's emulator diverges onto the normal screen and stacks repaint frames that read as history.
- Touch reuses the wheel policy. TerminalWheelController already decides the three cases; a finger drag adapts into its event shape rather than growing a second policy.
- Leaving the viewport is a state the person can get stuck in, so a return-to-live control is part of the decision, not a later polish.

Records to reconcile: ADR-052:72-73 states as a consequence that 'the scrollback layer draws above the grid exactly as it does under ADR-050'. Amend that consequence; the rest of ADR-052 stands, and the Away size rule it establishes is unaffected. ADR-050 introduced the layer in implementation rather than in the record, so it needs no amendment beyond a pointer.

State explicitly that the page reads where the viewport is (viewportY) and never what it says. That keeps the return-to-live control clear of ADR-019 and ADR-051's ban on screen inspection for attention: position is not content.
design: One record, not two. The theme plumbing (hvir-w00 sibling) rides as a bead: inheriting the desktop's palette has no contested alternative worth a record.
acceptance_criteria: docs/adr/ADR-053-*.md exists in the repo's ADR shape, carrying the decision, the rejected alternatives (page-owned span renderer; reflowed transcript; snap-to-live on output; a touch policy separate from the wheel policy), and the consequences. ADR-052's consequence at :72-73 is amended to point at it.

title: The PTY output tail drops sticky terminal modes, so every replay diverges from the session
description:
A reattaching emulator is fed `PtyOutputTail`, a flat 256 KB character window over the PTY stream (pty-output-tail.ts:2) that drops the oldest characters with no escape awareness. The sequences that set a terminal's sticky modes are emitted once, at program start, and then scroll out of that window. The worst case is the alternate screen: a full-screen harness writes \x1b[?1049h once, so for any session that has since produced 256 KB of output the replay begins on the normal screen while the session is on the alternate. The replay is not sometimes wrong; for a long-running full-screen session it is always wrong.

Observed through the Companion (hvir-w00). The phone's emulator, fed this tail, held Claude Code's full-screen repaints in its normal buffer, where they accumulated as scrollback: a thousand rows of successive redraws of one screen, complete with the feedback prompt, the 'Crunched for 37 s' status line, spinner frames and box borders, presented to the reader as if it were session history. The desktop showed a full-screen program with no scrollback at all, which is what a fullscreen harness actually has.

Both consumers are affected. pty-output-tail.ts:1 states the budget is 'shared by the renderer replay and the mirror tail', so the desktop's own reattach replay carries the same defect; it surfaces less because a live desktop pane rarely replays.

Approach (fixed 2026-09-19): scan the retained stream for the sticky modes a reattached emulator cannot guess, keep the current set as state independent of the byte window, and emit it as a preamble ahead of the tail. Pure and unit-testable, lives beside the tail in main where the stream is, and fixes both consumers at once. 1049 is the one that matters most; settle the rest of the set while implementing (bracketed paste 2004, application cursor keys, mouse tracking modes, and anything else whose absence changes how the replayed bytes are interpreted).

Rejected: asking the desktop renderer's emulator for isAlternateScreen(). That puts main's replay correctness behind a renderer round-trip and fails exactly when the renderer is hidden or throttled, against ADR-001 and ADR-014.

Also noted while diagnosing, not necessarily this bead's to fix: the same raw slice can cut a CSI sequence in half, so the first bytes a replayed emulator sees may be a fragment.
design: A sticky-mode scanner beside PtyOutputTail in src/main/pty. The tail keeps bytes; the scanner keeps mode state; the replay is preamble + tail. Do not widen the tail's budget to try to retain the enter sequence: the window is a memory bound, not a correctness mechanism, and anchoring it to the last mode change is unbounded.
acceptance_criteria: A session that has produced more than the tail budget in output, on the alternate screen, replays onto the alternate screen: a fresh emulator fed the replay reports isAlternateScreen() true and holds no scrollback. A unit test drives the scanner over a stream whose mode-setting prefix has been dropped and asserts the preamble restores it. The desktop's reattach replay path uses the same preamble.
notes: Found while grilling hvir-w00 on 2026-09-19. hvir-w00's implementation children depend on this: until it lands, no honest capture of a full-screen session's mirror is possible, because every capture records the divergence rather than the session.

title: Mock the phone history view in HTML and align on the design
description:
Design the phone's history view as standalone HTML before touching the Companion, and iterate on it with the maintainer until the shape is agreed.

Work in three steps.

1. Capture real data. Take the rows the page actually has to render, not invented text: dump CompanionTerminalPane.bufferLines() output for a real Claude Code turn and for a plain shell, as JSON (text plus the wrapped flag per row), into a fixture the mocks load. Do this from a test or a scratch harness against a recorded session; do not hand-write the sample. While capturing, settle the missing-space question with evidence: compare the captured row text against what the desktop terminal shows for the same turn, and say where the spaces go. Record the finding in this bead so it is not re-derived.

2. Mock. Build standalone HTML pages under a scratch or docs path, opened in a phone-width viewport, that render the captured fixture. Produce at least two shape-distinct treatments, not two coats of paint on one idea, for example:
   - terminal fidelity: keep the grid's columns, font and theme, carry colour and attributes across the seam, and let the column be a true continuation of the screen below it;
   - reflowed reading: use the wrapped flag to rejoin lines the desktop broke, set the text at the phone's width in a proportional or narrower monospace size, and treat the history as a transcript rather than a screen.
   Each mock shows the same captured turn so they can be compared directly. Include the chrome question in each: show what the view does with the feedback prompt, the status line, spinners and box borders.

3. Align and hand off. Iterate with the maintainer on the mocks until one is chosen. Write down the chrome rule in words precise enough to implement. If the chosen design means the page decides what terminal content means, draft the ADR for it rather than smuggling the rule into a component. Then file the implementation children against this epic, sized as independently reviewable units, and close this bead with the chosen mock and the diagnosis recorded.

Out of scope: any change under src/renderer/companion, src/main/companion, or the pane seam. This bead produces a decision and mocks, not shipped behaviour. The one exception is the read-only capture harness needed for step 1, which may be a test or a scratch script.
acceptance_criteria: A captured fixture of real bufferLines output exists for a Claude Code turn and a plain shell; the cause of the missing spaces is diagnosed with evidence and recorded on the bead; at least two shape-distinct HTML mocks render that fixture at phone width; the maintainer chose one; the harness-chrome rule is written in implementable words; an ADR is drafted if the rule decides what terminal content means; implementation children are filed against the epic.
notes:
Superseded by the 2026-09-19 design session (see hvir-w00 notes). Both things this bead existed to produce were reached from source instead:

The missing-space diagnosis: ghostty-web's translateToString concatenates per-cell getChars() and returns '' for codepoint 0 without padding (ghostty-web.js:4147), so blank cells vanish and take their columns with them. The desktop already builds row text cell by cell for this reason (ghostty-terminal-pane.ts:759-763). No capture was needed; the bug is in the library's source and the workaround is in this repo's.

The design fork the mocks were to answer: settled as fidelity, and then settled further as fidelity by deletion. The read-back becomes the emulator's own viewport (hvir-w00.3, recorded in ADR-053), which no HTML mock can reproduce honestly, and which is a smaller change than mocking it because it is mostly removal. The phone check moved to a verification step on hvir-w00.3, done against a real session, with the option to stop there if it feels wrong in the hand.

The chrome rule this bead was to write in implementable words turned out not to be needed: the chrome was replay divergence (hvir-coq), not content the page has to interpret.
close_reason: Superseded by hvir-w00.2 (ADR-053), hvir-w00.3 (read-back), hvir-w00.4 (return to live), hvir-w00.5 (theme) and hvir-coq (replay divergence). The diagnosis and the design decision it existed to produce were reached from source; the mocks would have prototyped a design nobody is building.

title: The Companion mirror's history column is unreadable on the phone
description:
Why: with a mirror open the live grid at the bottom of the phone renders correctly, but the scrollback column above it does not. Three separate defects were observed on a real phone against a Claude Code session on 2026-09-19.

1. Words lose the spaces between them. The column reads "Ididverifytheonethinginthatreply" where the terminal shows "I did verify the one thing in that reply". Whatever the cause, the text as drawn is close to unparseable.
2. The column is flat white on black while the grid below it carries the terminal's theme, so the two halves do not read as one surface even though they are meant to.
3. The text carries the harness's own TUI chrome, which means nothing to a person reading on a phone: a "How is claude doing this session?" feedback prompt, a "Crunched for 37 s" status line, spinners, and box-drawing borders. The phone shows everything the emulator holds, including the parts that only made sense as a full-screen layout on a desktop.

The first is a bug. The second and third are design questions that need a person's eye before any code changes, which is why the first child is an HTML mock rather than an implementation.

Structural facts (mapped 2026-09-19, all on feat/beads-panel):
- The column is one <pre> element. companion-terminal-mount.ts:79-83 creates it as .companion-terminal-history and appends it above the grid box in the same surface.
- companion-mirror-history.ts:19-21 builds its content: lines.map(line => line.text).join('\n'), written with textContent at most every 80 ms (HISTORY_REFRESH_MS), keeping a view that was at the newest line at the newest line.
- The rows come from the CompanionTerminalPane seam. companion-terminal-pane.ts:20-25 defines CompanionBufferLine as { text, wrapped }: text only, no colour, no attributes. The `wrapped` flag is carried across the seam and never used by the history text, so the emulator already tells the page where the desktop broke a line and the page ignores it.
- ghostty-companion-pane.ts:96-105 produces those rows with line.translateToString(false) over the active buffer.
- companion-terminal-mount.ts:213-216 takes every row before the screen's own rows as the scrollback, bounded by HISTORY_LINE_LIMIT (1000).
- styles.css:439-443 is the whole presentation: margin 0, color #e8eaee, white-space pre. The colour is hardcoded and is the one piece of the mirror that ignores the terminal theme.
- fit() at companion-terminal-mount.ts:228-238 scales the history with the grid by the same fitWidthScale transform, so while the desktop holds the size the column is drawn at the desktop's width and then shrunk. While the phone holds the size under ADR-052 it is drawn at the phone's own grid unscaled.

Open questions for the design session, none of them settled:
- What is actually removing the spaces? translateToString(false) is documented in this codebase as keeping the width, so either that is not what it does in ghostty-web, or the harness positions its text with cursor moves and never writes the intervening cells, or something downstream collapses them. Diagnose from captured data before designing around it.
- Which sessions does this view even apply to? A Claude Code session with tui=fullscreen draws on the alternate screen and has no scrollback at all (see the alternate-screen memory and ADR-052), so history above the grid should be empty for it. The strings observed are Claude Code's, so either that session was not in fullscreen mode, or what is showing is the primary buffer from before or after the alternate screen. The answer changes what the view is for.
- How much may the phone reinterpret what the terminal drew? Suppressing or demoting harness chrome means the page is reading content and deciding what it means. ADR-019 and ADR-051 forbid screen inspection for attention; display is not attention, and ADR-050 puts emulation on the phone by design, but the boundary should be stated in a record rather than assumed. If the answer is a rule rather than a tweak, this needs an ADR.
- Does the column keep terminal fidelity (colour, attributes, monospace columns) or become reflowed prose sized for a phone? Those are different products. The mock is how we find out which one is wanted.
design:

title: Companion mirror owns the PTY size while the desktop is Away (ADR-052)
description:
Why: a Claude Code session in fullscreen TUI mode (the user's ~/.claude/settings.json sets "tui": "fullscreen") draws on the alternate screen, so the emulator has no scrollback. On the phone the mirror can only show the desktop's grid scaled to the phone's width: a short strip pinned at the bottom with black above it, nothing to scroll, and the conversation history unreachable. Verified 2026-09-18 by spawning claude in a pty and seeing CSI ?1049h. Blink.sh avoids this by being the terminal: the PTY is sized to the phone. tmux faces the same two-client question and answers it with window-size (smallest / latest / manual).

Decision (user approved 2026-09-18): the phone owns the PTY's size while the desktop is Away. A mirror opened while no hvir window is focused resizes the PTY to the phone's own grid, so a full-screen program lays out for the phone and fills it. When any desktop window gains focus the desktop reclaims: its fit controller resizes the PTY back and the phone returns to the scaled-mirror view it has today. Away is the existing ActionableAttentionSet.away() signal that already gates Push, so the rule the user learns is one they know: away means the phone is the terminal.

Rejected: phone owns the size whenever a mirror is open regardless of focus (tmux latest; squashes the desktop while you sit at it with the phone beside you); an explicit 'take the size' control on the phone (one more control on a page that was just stripped to one view, and a tap every time); scaling rows to the phone's height and panning sideways (the removed fill-height view); resizing nothing and only paging the program with PageUp/PageDown from a drag (leaves the black area).

Defaults taken: while the phone holds the size the desktop draws the grid at the phone's dimensions in the top-left of its pane, remainder blank, with a one-line notice (as tmux marks a smaller client). The phone uses a fixed readable font and derives cols/rows from its terminal area, recomputed on orientation change and keyboard show. When two phones hold the same PTY the most recent resize wins. ADR-052 partially supersedes ADR-050's 'never resizes the PTY' clause (ADR-050 lines 37-38, 46-47; revisit clause 112-115) and pty-contract.ts:148.

Structural facts (mapped 2026-09-18): main records geometry per entry (pty-supervisor.ts entry.geometry, updated only in resize(); publishGeometry reaches mirrors only). Desktop resize: TerminalFitController (ghostty-terminal-fit.ts) -> terminal-runtime.ts pty:resize -> main/ipc/features/terminal.ts -> PtySupervisor.resize gated by requireOwned. No pty:geometry event back to the renderer exists; TerminalPane has no fixed-size mode (fit only stops under presentation 'hidden'). Mirror lease reads geometry once at attach and forwards onGeometry while live; lease has no resize. Focus: electron-window-manager.ts -> ApplicationAttention.setOwnerFocused -> ActionableAttentionSet.away().

Children are the seams: ADR, supervisor door + arbitration, renderer geometry event + held-size pane, phone fit + resize request, docs + device verification.

title: Terminal notification prompts as actionable attention with their message, on the desktop and the phone
description:
## Motivation

A harness blocked on a permission prompt and a harness that finished its turn both show as Ready (quiet after Enter, ADR-019). The person cannot tell which sessions need a decision, on the desktop Sessions view or the Companion page. Once a row is Ready it stays Ready until desktop focus, so a second prompt in the same session is invisible, and a prompt answered from the phone mirror leaves the row flagged.

Claude Code with preferredNotifChannel iterm2 writes OSC 9 into the PTY a few seconds after a permission prompt appears (body: Claude needs your permission) and when it finishes a turn (Claude is waiting for your input). Probed on 2026-09-18 with Claude Code 2.1.277 under TERM_PROGRAM=hvir: the sequence arrived about 6 s after the prompt, the terminal was silent meanwhile. hvir's pane already translates OSC 9 / OSC 777 into a notification event with title and body (ghostty-terminal-events.ts) and then collapses it into a bell in terminal-pane-event-coordinator.ts, dropping the body.

## What this epic does

Governing record: ADR-051. A terminal notification raises a prompt attention immediately (no arming, no quiet wait) carrying its bounded body; the body crosses renderer actionable entries, main's actionable set, the Sessions projection row, the Companion row, and the Push line. A prompt entry outranks Ready and Bell; a later notification replaces the body. Clearing: desktop focus (ADR-009) and, for the prompt entry only, input from the Companion mirror. Output resuming never clears it. OSC 9 stops mapping to bell; BEL stays the bell. hvir does not set the harness's notification channel; the runbook documents it.

## Children

1. Attention model and contracts: prompt kind with body end to end (renderer state, shared contract, main set, sessions projection, companion rows, push describe), mirror-input clearing, tests.
2. Surfaces: terminal rail badge, desktop Sessions view, Companion list row and mirror header, push line, smoke probe variant, tests.
3. Docs: runbook section (setting, delay, what each surface shows), design.md index entry and notices, COMPASS notes.

Order: 1, then 2, then 3.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A Claude Code permission prompt in an hvir terminal shows within seconds as a prompt with its message on the terminal row, the desktop Sessions view, the Companion list, and the mirror view
- [ ] A second prompt in the same session shows again without a desktop focus in between
- [ ] Answering from the phone mirror clears the prompt entry; Ready and Bell are unaffected by phone input
- [ ] A notification body never exceeds its bound at any boundary and is validated on the wire
- [ ] Sessions with a harness that emits no notification keep the ADR-019 Ready behavior exactly
- [ ] npm run verify passes; the attention-away smoke proves a prompt entry with its body reaches main while Away

That is nearly every session we run. Claude Code and Codex are started from a shell
inside an hvir terminal, and gas city workers are joined with `gc session attach`
inside an hvir terminal. On the desktop, Interact on such a row borrows the live
terminal pane with the whole keyboard. On the phone the same row is a dead end, and
the moment that matters most, a permission prompt or option picker waiting in
Claude Code's terminal UI, exists only on that screen. No transcript file carries it.

## What this epic does

A Companion page can select a live hvir-owned terminal row and see that terminal,
rendered on the phone by ghostty-web at the desktop's geometry, from a retained tail
of output onward. With typing allowed in Settings and armed on the page, keystrokes
return to that exact PTY instance. A prompt submitted from the phone still produces
the next Ready and the next Push, because the renderer keeps classifying. Nothing
changes on the desktop: one owner per PTY, no new clearing rule, no resize from the
phone.

Governing record: ADR-050, which partially supersedes ADR-049's exclusion of a
terminal screen and terminal input from the Companion.

## The seams, and why this is not an escalation

Main already sees every PTY byte. `PtyStreamAttachment` holds a set of data
listeners and fans output out to all of them; only the public door,
`PtySupervisor.attach`, is gated on the renderer owner and generation through
`requireOwned`. The replay buffer (`MAX_INITIAL_REPLAY_LENGTH`, 256 K chars) is
consumed when the renderer attaches, so a second reader gets nothing today; a
retained tail is the one new piece of state. Writes already go through
`PtySupervisor.write` under the same gate, so a mirror write is a second caller of
an existing authority bound to an instance rather than an owner.

The Sessions projection already carries the identity the mirror needs: a live row's
`livePty.handle` is the PTY `instanceId`, and its row handle is the PTY id. The
Companion sessions service already holds one demand owner per page
(`kind: 'companion'`), opens and closes pages on the SSE stream, and closes every
page on revocation. Mirror leases hang off that lifecycle.

The phone page is a second Vite entry served from the Companion's flat asset
bundle. ghostty-web loads its WebAssembly through a Vite `?url` import, so the
module is already emitted into that bundle. Two things block it on the phone today:
the asset allowlist in `companion-assets.ts` and `companion-http.ts` has no `.wasm`
content type, and the page CSP in `src/renderer/companion/index.html` lacks
`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.

ADR-017, ADR-026, and ADR-032 forbid hvir composing text into a PTY. Phone
keystrokes are the user's exact bytes, uncomposed and unappended, bound to an exact
instance that fails closed on change. Those records are untouched.

## Decisions taken before decomposition

- Mirror, not transfer. The renderer stays the PTY's owner; the mirror is bound to
  the instance and survives a renderer document swap, ending only on PTY exit, page
  close, revocation, shutdown, or reselect.
- Bytes cross uninterpreted. Main keeps a tail and forwards; the phone emulates.
  No headless emulator in main.
- Geometry follows the desktop. The phone renders the desktop's columns and rows,
  scaled to fit, and never resizes the PTY.
- Typing is opt-in three times: a Settings permission defaulting to off, per-mirror
  arming on the page, and disarming on hide, lease end, or inactivity.
- Attention stays in the renderer. Main notifies the owning renderer of mirror
  input so ADR-019 arming happens where it always has. No phone action clears
  attention.
- Eligibility equals the desktop's Interact: live, connected, live PTY. External
  rows without an hvir terminal keep the transcript path.
- Transport reuses what exists: mirror output rides the page's SSE stream as a new
  event type; input rides bounded POST bodies. A socket is a later optimization,
  not a decision.

## Child issues

1. PTY supervisor: retained output tail and a mirror lease door on an exact
   instance. Tail retention in `PtyStreamAttachment` independent of renderer
   replay; `attachMirror(instanceId, handlers)` returning a lease with `write`,
   geometry on attach and on change, ending on exit; tests at the supervisor
   altitude including the fail-closed cases.
2. Companion service and routes: one mirror lease per page, `select` on an
   eligible live row opens it, a `terminal` SSE event carries tail, bytes, and
   geometry, `POST /api/sessions/:handle/input` writes under the lease, and
   page close, reselect, and revocation release it.
3. Phone page: terminal view in ghostty-web through the engine-neutral pane seam,
   `.wasm` in the asset allowlist and CSP, fit-to-width scaling, on-screen keys
   (Enter, Escape, Tab, arrows, Ctrl-C), arm and disarm controls, and the
   `not-projected` dead end replaced by the same plain wording the desktop uses.
4. Settings and attention: the typing permission in Settings > Companion with its
   status, the mirror-input notice from main to the owning renderer recorded as
   terminal input, and a smoke scenario proving a phone-submitted prompt yields
   Ready and Push while Away under background throttling.
5. Docs: operator runbook section for the mirror and typing permission, ADR index
   entries (already drafted with ADR-050), and the Companion COMPASS.

Order: 1 first; 2 and 3 in parallel on 1; 4 on 2; 5 last.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Selecting a live hvir terminal row on the phone shows that terminal's screen,
      including a Claude Code permission prompt that is on the desktop's screen
- [ ] The mirror survives a desktop reload of the renderer document and ends when
      the PTY exits, the page closes, or pairing is revoked
- [ ] With typing disallowed in Settings, no input route accepts bytes; with it
      allowed but unarmed on the page, no keystroke reaches the PTY
- [ ] An armed Enter from the phone answers a Claude Code prompt on the desktop,
      and the row leaves the actionable set when output resumes
- [ ] A prompt submitted from the phone produces the next Ready and one Push while
      Away, with the desktop window hidden and throttled
- [ ] The phone never resizes the PTY; the desktop's geometry is what the phone
      renders
- [ ] Mirror bytes never appear in logs, diagnostics, or push text
- [ ] Rows without a live hvir PTY keep their existing transcript or unavailable
      path, with a plain sentence instead of a reason code

title: Return to live from a scrolled-back mirror
description:
Once the emulator's viewport is the read-back (hvir-w00.3), a person who scrolls up stays there: ghostty keeps its viewport while output arrives, which is the right behaviour (losing your place mid-read is worse than missing a line) but leaves no way to notice the session moved and no quick way back. A phone viewport is a few dozen rows against a thousand rows of scrollback, and there is no scrollbar to grab.

Show one control, only while the viewport is off the bottom, that says the session has moved and returns to live in one tap.

The page reads where the viewport is (viewportY) and never what it says. That is position, not content, so it stays clear of ADR-019 and ADR-051's ban on screen inspection for attention; ADR-053 states the boundary.
design: One control, one piece of state, appearing on a condition the emulator already exposes. No unread marker and no record of what arrived while away: that is a second piece of state plus a rule for when it clears, and nobody has asked for it.
acceptance_criteria: Scrolling back from live shows the control; returning to the bottom hides it. Tapping it puts the viewport at live. Output arriving while scrolled back does not move the viewport. Nothing about the control reads the screen's text.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: all five gates pass (check-adrs, check-seams, lint, typecheck, 469 files / 4130 tests). Every new test was mutation-probed against the source it pins. Three adversarial findings confirmed and repaired, six refuted; the repair also deleted viewportOffset() and releaseViewport as dead by construction.

title: The mirror inherits the desktop's terminal theme
description:
The phone's emulator has never seen the desktop's palette. createGhosttyCompanionPane passes no theme, so it runs ghostty-web's built-in default; grep for 'theme' across src/renderer/companion, src/main/companion and src/shared/sessions-companion.ts returns nothing. The desktop applies the user's TerminalColorTheme (ghostty-terminal-pane.ts:57, :327).

This is the real shape of hvir-w00's second observed defect. The epic read it as a themed grid beside an unthemed history column; in fact neither was themed, and the clash was the history <pre>'s hardcoded #e8eaee against a different unthemed palette. Deleting the <pre> (hvir-w00.3) removes the clash and leaves the mirror on the wrong palette.

Carry the desktop's theme to the mirror and apply it. The mirror should look like the session it mirrors: a person glancing at their phone should recognise their own terminal.

Plumbing, to settle while implementing:
- TerminalColorTheme and normalizeTerminalColorTheme live in src/renderer/src/terminal/ (terminal-pane.ts:20, terminal-palette.ts:70), which the page may not import. They are pure data and a pure function; move them to src/shared, where the page already imports from.
- The companion wire carries the theme, validated at the boundary like every other field in sessions-companion.ts.
- Where main learns the selected theme is an open question: the catalog and selection live in the desktop renderer today. Answer it before designing the wire field.

Rejected: a deliberate phone-tuned palette independent of the desktop's. It permanently makes the mirror look like a different terminal, which is the opposite of what a mirror is for.
design: No phone-side override and no settings surface for it: that is a precedence rule nobody has asked for. Inherit, full stop.
acceptance_criteria: A mirror opened against a session on a non-default theme draws in that theme, live screen and scrollback alike. The palette type and normalizer are in src/shared with no renderer dependency. The wire field is validated at the page boundary. Changing the desktop's theme while a mirror is open is covered one way or the other: either it follows, or the bead records why it does not.
notes:
BLOCKED and deferred out of hvir-w00's critical path on 2026-09-19, with evidence from the grounding pass.

Main cannot see the selected palette at all. The theme ids live in the desktop renderer's localStorage under 'hvir:settings:v1' (src/renderer/src/settings/settings.ts:32) and the appearance under 'hvir:theme' (src/renderer/src/theme.ts:7), resolved to a palette per TerminalView at src/renderer/src/terminal/TerminalView.tsx:111-112. src/shared/ipc/companion.ts:9-20 carries only config read/save, pairing issue/revoke and status-changed; src/main/companion/companion-config-store.ts:24-30 persists only enabled, port, mirrorInputAllowed, credential and push. The only main-side read of that storage anywhere in the repo is localStorage.getItem('hvir:settings:v1') inside executeJavaScript in the smoke harness (src/main/smoke/renderer-lifecycle.ts:18,22,106), which is test scaffolding, not a production path.

So this bead is not 'apply a palette'. It is: a renderer to main publish channel (registered in src/main/ipc/features/terminal.ts, the only place ipc.handleSend exists, at :466-484, already 547 lines), a per-PTY palette store in main with a forget-on-exit hook, the publisher moved to src/renderer/src/terminal/terminal-runtime.ts (terminal-runtime-live-settings.ts cannot do it: its functions take only (pane, options) and never touch window.hvir), the palette type and normalizer moved to src/shared, and a new required field on the companion wire.

It also trips the architecture gate twice. scripts/architecture-hotspots.json:215-233 pins sha256 provenance for both scripts/generate-terminal-theme-catalog.mts and src/renderer/src/terminal/terminal-color-schema.mts; moving or editing either makes scripts/architecture-inventory.mts:288-300 throw 'Generated input identity mismatch' and fails npm run architecture:check. Rewriting the inputs path to fix it is classified as a relaxation by scripts/architecture-policy.mts:362-368, which ADR-040:75-91 says a consuming issue's review cannot authorize. Separately, .mts under src/shared is in neither tsconfig (tsconfig.web.json:9-15 lists src/shared/**/*.ts and src/renderer/**/*.mts, never src/shared/**/*.mts), so eslint's projectService errors on it.

Nothing regresses by deferring: the mirror stays on ghostty-web's default palette, which is what it does today. Before this is picked up it needs the architecture relaxation authorized on its own terms, and a decision on whether a live desktop theme change propagates to an open mirror (a 'theme' CompanionTerminalEvent variant modelled on 'geometry' would be safe, since companion-wire.ts:65-69 ignores unknown event names).

title: Companion mirror: one fit-to-width view with scrollback above a bottom-pinned grid
description: The mirror offers three views (reflow, fit width, fill height). Only the fit-width layout is wanted: scrollback drawn above the desktop's grid, scaled to the phone's width, the host scrolling over the two. The reflow page also leaks under the grid in the fit-width view because its display:flex rule overrides the hidden attribute, so the black area below the grid shows reflow text. Remove the other two views and the view control, pin the grid to the host's bottom edge when the column is shorter than the host, and update runbook and compass.
close_reason: Single fit-to-width view with scrollback above a bottom-pinned grid; reflow and fill-height removed
